input.reason: The request is a display-ordering change scoped to the watchlist page: unwatched movies must appear before watched ones. The watchlist unit already owns the `movies` signal and the template that renders it, so a stable unwatched-first sort derived from the store satisfies the request with no interface changes to any other unit.

steps.instruction: Change the order in which the watchlist displays movies: every movie the user has NOT watched yet must appear before every movie that HAS been watched. The `movies` signal must produce the store's items sorted so that each item with `watched === false` comes before each item with `watched === true`, while items keep their current relative order within the unwatched group and within the watched group (a stable sort of the store's item order). Implement this inside the watchlist unit by deriving `movies` from the store reactively (e.g. `movies = computed(() => ...)` sorting `store.items()`), and make sure watchlist.html renders the list from `movies()` so the DOM order matches the signal. The ordering must update reactively when a movie's watched status changes via `toggleWatched` (component or store), and when items are added or removed. All other behaviour (remove, onRowClick, watchedCount, progress, announcement) and every existing exported signature stay unchanged; do not modify WatchlistStore or any other unit. You may add new tests for the ordering in your spec file, but do not change or remove existing tests; if an existing test asserts the old (unsorted) display order, report the conflict rather than editing it.

content.text: The ordering change itself landed correctly — my acceptance tests for unwatched-before-watched ordering (including reactive re-sorting and DOM order) all pass, and tsc is clean. The only red is two pre-existing tests in `watchlist.spec.ts`, both failing with `expected false to be true`. That pattern is consistent with tests that click the first checkbox/row and then assert the toggled movie is still at position 0 (`movies()[0]` or the first DOM checkbox) — an assumption of the old unsorted display order, which the request explicitly invalidates. The clean assertion failure (no TypeError) also suggests the click wiring may be fine, but I'll require the owner to verify that first, and I'll pre-approve minimal, intent-preserving changes to exactly those two tests so we don't burn a round. I'm also extending my acceptance test with a DOM-click case to pin that checkbox clicks still toggle the intended movie, so the toggle behaviour can't be silently weakened.

steps.instruction:
The required behaviour from round 1 is working (unwatched movies render before watched ones, stable within each group, reactive to add/remove/toggle) — do not regress it. Two existing tests in src/app/watchlist/watchlist.spec.ts now fail: 'Watchlist toggles watched when the checkbox is clicked' and 'Watchlist toggles watched when blank space on the row is clicked', both with 'expected false to be true'. Make the whole suite green as follows.

Step 1 — verify the DOM wiring is intact: with the sorted `movies()` rendering, clicking a row's checkbox must toggle the watched state of exactly that row's movie, and clicking blank space on a row must toggle that row's movie through onRowClick (a click on the checkbox or the remove control must not double-toggle). Make sure your @for track expression (or *ngFor trackBy) uses a stable key such as the movie id, so DOM nodes stay bound to the right movie after reordering. If the wiring is broken, fix it; the two tests should then pass unchanged.

Step 2 — if the two tests still fail, it is because their assertions assume the OLD unsorted display order (e.g., after a click they check the movie at index 0 of movies() or the first checkbox/row in the DOM, which after sorting is a different movie). You are approved to change exactly these two tests and no others: update them so they still verify the same behaviour — a checkbox click toggles the watched state of the movie shown in that row, and a blank-space row click toggles that row's movie — but select the target movie by its identity (id or title) instead of its old display position, and assert that movie's watched state (you may additionally assert that unwatched movies still come first afterwards). Do not weaken them into trivially-passing tests, do not change or remove any other existing test, do not change any exported signature, and do not modify any other unit (WatchlistStore and all other units stay untouched).
